P1.description: Enforce authorization checks on every request to protected resources, including AJAX, server-side, and background calls

P2.description: Adopt a deny-by-default strategy: explicitly grant permissions, deny everything not expressly allowed

P3.description: Centralize authorization logic instead of scattering checks throughout controllers and services

P4.description: Perform access control only on the server side; never rely on client-side logic

P5.description: Define clear trust boundaries, user types, resources, and allowed operations during design

P6.description: Ensure authorization decisions are consistent and globally enforced via middleware, not ad-hoc checks

P7.description: Avoid exposing raw identifiers; prefer lookups based on the authenticated user's identity

P8.description: Handle failed access checks safely and consistently; never leak sensitive info in error messages

P9.description: Enforce per-object authorization checks for every access

P10.description: Prefer indirect references (opaque tokens/mapping tables) instead of direct database IDs

P11.description: Scope lookups to resources owned/permitted for the current user

P12.description: Use non-sequential, hard-to-guess identifiers as defense-in-depth

P13.description: Distinguish clearly between authentication and transaction authorization

P14.description: Ensure users can view/verify significant transaction data before approving

P15.description: Enforce transaction authorization server-side; validate all transaction data server-side

P16.description: Use the framework's built-in CSRF protection or add CSRF tokens to state-changing requests

P17.description: Use synchronizer token pattern (stateful) or double submit cookies (stateless)

P18.description: Ensure CSRF tokens are unique per session, secret, and cryptographically unpredictable

P19.description: Never use GET for state-changing operations

P20.description: Consider SameSite attributes, custom headers, origin/Referer validation as defense-in-depth

P21.description: Validate, canonicalize and restrict all user-supplied file paths; resolve symlinks/hard links before any file-access decision and compare against an allowlisted base directory

P22.description: Reject '../' sequences, absolute paths, and encoded traversal payloads; never build file paths by direct string concatenation with user input

P23.description: Before opening/serving a file, resolve any symbolic or hard link to its final target and verify that target is still inside the permitted directory

P24.description: Never place files with sensitive data (config, credentials, backups) inside a web-accessible directory or under the web root

P25.description: Disable directory listing on web servers and application frameworks by default

P26.description: Never log, display in errors, or otherwise expose sensitive information to unauthorized actors; classify data to decide what may be returned to a given caller

P27.description: Do not hardcode secrets or sensitive information in source code or source code comments

P28.description: Use secure APIs for temporary file creation (unique, unpredictable names, restrictive permissions); clean up after use and never create temp files in world-writable directories

P29.description: Apply correct default permissions and explicit ownership checks to all created files/directories; verify ownership before privileged operations

P30.description: Validate any redirect/forward target against an allowlist of trusted destinations; never redirect using a raw unvalidated URL parameter

P31.description: Do not transmit private/internal resources or system information to a different trust sphere without explicit authorization and minimization

P32.description: Remove or disable exposed debugging methods, administrative functions, or dangerous APIs in production builds

P33.description: Treat SSRF as an access-control problem: validate and allowlist destination hosts/IPs for any server-initiated request

P34.description: Integrate security plugins/static analysis for IaC into the workflow

P35.description: Perform threat modeling on IaC to identify high-risk resources

P36.description: Manage secrets properly in IaC; never hardcode tokens/passwords/keys

P37.description: Apply least privilege to IaC scripts and inventories

P38.description: Maintain accurate inventory management for provisioning/decommissioning

P40.description: Enable secure error logging; do not expose errors directly to users

P41.description: Configure secure session settings (strict mode, secure/httponly/samesite cookies)

P42.description: Prevent PHP execution in upload dirs; restrict open_basedir

P43.description: Do not expose the Docker daemon over unauthenticated TCP

P45.description: Use Linux security modules (Seccomp, AppArmor, SELinux); don't disable default profile

P46.description: Run containers with a read-only filesystem unless write access is strictly necessary

P47.description: Define non-root USER in Dockerfiles; pin base image/OS package versions

P48.description: Enforce encrypted transport (TLS) for all data transmission at the framework/platform level; disable cleartext fallbacks

P49.description: Never allow externally-controlled input to alter system or application configuration settings at runtime

P50.description: Disable XML external entity (XXE) processing and DTD/entity expansion by default in all XML parsers; use the least-capable parser configuration needed

P51.description: Restrict cross-domain policies (CORS, crossdomain.xml) to an explicit allowlist of trusted origins; never use wildcard origins for sensitive endpoints

P52.description: Enforce strict server-side model/input validation in web frameworks; never rely on client-side or implicit framework validation alone

P53.description: Update vulnerable dependencies in a test environment and run automated tests before deploying

P54.description: Apply vendor workarounds and protect impacted functions with I/O validation

P55.description: Create unit tests mimicking the vulnerability to confirm patches remain effective

P56.description: Document temporary workarounds and CVE handling; scope tool suppressions to the specific CVE

P57.description: Vet third-party npm modules: review health, credibility, changelogs before adoption

P58.description: Delay immediate upgrades; observe for reported issues before updating

P59.description: Disable lifecycle scripts by default to reduce arbitrary code execution during install

P60.description: Scan dependencies for vulnerabilities; monitor manifests (SCA/SBOM)

P61.description: Sign build artifacts and provenance so consumers can verify integrity

P62.description: Use access-controlled registries/mirrors; rotate CI/publisher tokens

P63.description: Use a server-driven data layer for third-party JavaScript interaction

P64.description: Restrict allowed tag types in tag managers

P65.description: Enforce contractual requirements for third-party code security/integrity

P66.description: Use Subresource Integrity (SRI) and iframe containment for third-party JS

P67.description: Identify and replace use of obsolete, deprecated, or unsafe functions flagged by static analysis or vendor deprecation notices

P68.description: Do not store passwords using reversible encryption; use Argon2/PBKDF2/bcrypt/scrypt

P69.description: Use vetted algorithms only: AES >=128-bit, RSA/ECC >=2048-bit

P71.description: Do not implement cryptographic algorithms yourself; use well-reviewed libraries

P72.description: Use OS/framework/cloud secure storage mechanisms (HSM, KMS, key vaults)

P73.description: Never hardcode keys or check them into version control

P74.description: Store encryption keys separately; implement envelope encryption (DEK/KEK)

P75.description: Use a cryptographically secure random number generator (CSPRNG) for all security-relevant values; never seed PRNGs predictably or reuse seeds

P76.description: Generate a fresh, random IV/nonce for every encryption operation; never reuse a nonce or key pair

P77.description: Fully validate the certificate chain of trust to a trusted root CA before accepting a certificate; never skip this validation

P78.description: Encrypt all sensitive data and credentials in transit using TLS; never transmit them in cleartext

P79.description: Enforce expiration and rotation policies for cryptographic keys; reject operations using expired keys

P80.description: Do not use reversible encoding (e.g., Base64) as a substitute for proper password hashing

P81.description: Always perform full, correct verification of cryptographic signatures before trusting signed data or code

P82.description: Disable legacy/insecure cryptographic algorithms and protocols in negotiation; enforce a minimum secure cipher suite

P83.description: Use only well-vetted, standard cryptographic library implementations; avoid custom implementations of primitives

P84.description: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements for all database access

P85.description: Validate/sanitize untrusted input against strict allowlists

P86.description: Use ORM/query builders that enforce binding parameters

P87.description: Avoid direct OS command execution with untrusted data; prefer high-level APIs. If necessary, strictly validate and escape command arguments

P88.description: Use parameterized LDAP filters and encode special characters to prevent filter manipulation

P89.description: Perform context-appropriate output encoding (HTML, attribute, JavaScript, CSS, URL) for all untrusted data rendered into pages

P90.description: Avoid using untrusted data in innerHTML, document.write, or direct DOM insertion without proper encoding/sanitization

P91.description: Implement a restrictive Content Security Policy (CSP) to limit script sources and inline code

P92.description: Use parameterized XPath/XML queries and disable external entity resolution when processing untrusted XML or XPath expressions

P93.description: Neutralize CR/LF and other header-injection characters in user-controlled values written into HTTP headers, redirects, or logs; set headers via safe framework APIs

P94.description: Never pass untrusted input to eval(), dynamic code generation, or dynamically compiled/saved code

P95.description: Disable Server-Side Includes (SSI) where not required; strictly neutralize user input before SSI processing

P96.description: Never build file include/require paths from user input; restrict to an allowlist and disable remote file inclusion settings

P97.description: Validate and restrict user-controlled resource identifiers against an allowlist before use across trust spheres

P98.description: Ensure every framework validation hook (e.g., Struts ActionForm validate()) is fully implemented and consistently applied

P99.description: Validate all XML input against a strict schema with external entity resolution disabled before processing

P100.description: Never construct system commands, library search paths, or process arguments from unsanitized user input

P101.description: Validate array/index and numeric bounds before using user-controlled values to access arrays or buffers

P102.description: Explicitly define and test how the application handles unexpected/invalid special characters rather than relying on default behavior

P103.description: Never use externally-controlled input to select classes/methods for reflection; restrict to an allowlist of permitted classes

P104.description: Mark security-critical public/static fields as final/read-only so untrusted code cannot modify them after initialization

P105.description: Treat Expression Language/template/query-language expressions as code; never evaluate expressions built from unsanitized user input

P106.description: Perform structured threat modeling for new applications and significant changes

P107.description: Create accurate data-flow diagrams (DFDs), trust boundaries, actors, flows, assets

P108.description: Define abuse cases alongside use cases

P109.description: Conduct attack surface analysis; minimize unnecessary exposure

P110.description: Never construct file names or paths from externally-controlled input, even indirectly; always resolve against a fixed, validated base path

P111.description: Use strict allowlists (not denylists) to define what input is accepted for any validation rule

P112.description: Never store credentials in application code, configuration, or unprotected storage; use a dedicated secrets manager

P113.description: Assign privileges following least-privilege at design and runtime; verify grants/roles are explicit, reviewed, revocable

P114.description: Manage user accounts through a single, well-defined lifecycle process; never allow ad-hoc user management logic

P115.description: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in memory when feasible; never store sensitive information in cleartext

P116.description: Protect all concurrent access to shared resources with proper synchronization to prevent race conditions

P117.description: Avoid abrupt process termination calls (e.g., System.exit()) within shared/managed runtime environments

P118.description: Ensure primary communication channels used for security-critical operations are authenticated and protected against interception/tampering

P119.description: Restrict file uploads to expected types via content inspection (not just extension/MIME); store uploads outside the web root; rename uploaded files

P120.description: Configure servers/proxies consistently to avoid conflicting HTTP request interpretation; keep front-end and back-end parsers aligned

P121.description: Ensure the UI accurately represents security-critical information; never let styling obscure or misrepresent it

P122.description: Never initialize security-critical/trusted variables or data stores from external, unauthenticated sources

P123.description: Treat all web parameters as attacker-controlled, even ones assumed immutable (hidden fields, cookies); revalidate server-side on every use

P124.description: Explicitly define and enforce trust boundaries; never let data cross a boundary without validation appropriate to the more-trusted side

P125.description: Set appropriate cache-control headers to prevent browsers from caching pages with sensitive information

P126.description: Avoid storing sensitive information in persistent/long-lived cookies; if unavoidable, encrypt the value and minimize lifetime

P127.description: Never place sensitive data in URL query strings or use GET for requests carrying sensitive parameters

P128.description: Validate that function/API calls are invoked with the correct number, type, and order of arguments, especially at trust boundaries

P129.description: Do not allow external actors to modify critical application state data directly; mediate all state changes through validated server-side logic

P130.description: Apply compartmentalization: isolate components/tenants/privilege levels so compromise of one does not cascade

P131.description: Do not rely on secrecy of implementation as a security control; controls must remain effective even if publicly known

P132.description: Follow established secure design principles (least privilege, fail-safe defaults, defense in depth, complete mediation)

P133.description: Avoid use of known-dangerous functions; replace with safer, bounds-checked alternatives

P134.description: Regularly verify that protection mechanisms (filters, WAF rules, validation layers) are active and cannot be bypassed

P135.description: Implement rate limiting/throttling for security-sensitive interactions (login attempts, API calls, transactions)

P136.description: Never make a security decision based solely on untrusted input; corroborate with server-side, trusted state

P137.description: Enforce that multi-step workflows complete in the correct order and cannot be skipped or replayed out of sequence

P138.description: Use X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors to control iframe embedding and prevent clickjacking

P139.description: Add rel='noopener noreferrer' to links opening untrusted targets to prevent reverse tabnabbing via window.opener

P140.description: Require authentication for all pages/resources except explicitly public ones

P141.description: Use centralized authentication implementation/vetted libraries or IDPs

P142.description: Enforce minimum password length; allow all characters without arbitrary rules

P144.description: Avoid forcing periodic password changes; encourage strong passwords with strength meters

P145.description: Implement adaptive and multi-factor authentication for sensitive operations

P146.description: Implement account lockout with configurable thresholds and exponential backoff

P147.description: Never use hard-coded, empty, or default credentials in code, configuration, or shipped products; force change on first use

P148.description: Ensure exactly one server-validated authentication path exists; reject alternate paths, spoofed identity, replayed credentials, or client-supplied 'immutable' identity data

P149.description: Never use network-layer attributes (source IP, Referer header, reverse DNS) as an authentication factor

P150.description: Fully validate that a TLS certificate's hostname matches the connection target; never disable hostname verification

P151.description: Ensure communication channels used for authentication are accessible only to the intended endpoints

P152.description: Verify that every step defined in the authentication protocol actually executes in order and cannot be skipped

P153.description: Regenerate the session identifier on successful authentication and on privilege-level change

P154.description: Enforce idle and absolute session timeouts; invalidate sessions server-side on logout

P155.description: Require re-authentication before allowing a password or credential change

P156.description: Design account/password recovery flows with the same rigor as login: time-limited single-use tokens, notify owner of attempts

P157.description: Verify authenticity of both source and destination of a communication channel before trusting authentication data received on it

P158.description: Do not deserialize untrusted data; prefer JSON/XML when architecture permits
P158.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P159.description: Identify and review all endpoints that accept serialized data
P159.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P160.description: For Java, override resolveClass() to restrict which classes can be deserialized
P160.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P161.description: Replace generic readObject() with safer alternatives enforcing size/count limits
P161.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P162.description: Mark fields that must never be exposed during (de)serialization as private transient
P162.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P163.description: Avoid serializers where type is set by user-controlled variables (TypeNameHandling)
P163.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P164.description: Prefer pure data formats/serializers that don't support polymorphic type injection
P164.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P165.description: Verify authenticity/integrity of all downloaded code, updates, and data with digital signatures or checksums before use
P165.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P166.description: Set an explicit, fully-qualified search path for libraries/executables; never rely on an inherited or user-controllable search path
P166.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P167.description: Scan all code and dependencies for embedded malicious payloads as part of the build pipeline
P167.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P168.description: Never use client-side cookies as the sole basis for a security decision; protect integrity server-side (signed/encrypted cookies)
P168.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P169.description: Only load code/functionality from sources within your trust boundary; verify integrity of external functionality (SRI, signed packages)
P169.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P170.description: Never allow user input to directly set arbitrary object properties (mass assignment); bind only an explicit allowlist of fields
P170.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P171.description: On Android, explicitly set exported=false on components unless intentionally public; protect exported components with permissions
P171.owasp_category: A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures

P172.description: Ensure logs record when, where, who, and what for security-relevant events
P172.owasp_category: A09:2025 Security Logging and Alerting Failures

P173.description: Validate/sanitize event data to prevent log injection
P173.owasp_category: A09:2025 Security Logging and Alerting Failures

P174.description: Do not log private/secret information, source code, keys, or certificates
P174.owasp_category: A09:2025 Security Logging and Alerting Failures

P175.description: Ensure no security-relevant event data is silently dropped, truncated, or lost between generation and storage of logs
P175.owasp_category: A09:2025 Security Logging and Alerting Failures

P176.description: Centralize handling of exceptions/failed authorization; avoid unstable/partial states

P177.description: Avoid exposing stack traces/debug output in error responses; log securely, show generic messages

P178.description: Explicitly validate that all expected parameters are present and reject requests with unexpected extra parameters

P179.description: Catch and explicitly handle every exception a call can raise; check the return value of every function that can fail

P180.description: Explicitly handle insufficient-privilege conditions and fail closed (deny) rather than continuing with degraded checks

P181.description: Validate divisor/denominator values before arithmetic operations that could divide by zero

P182.description: Ensure every detected error condition triggers a defined handling action; detecting an error and doing nothing is itself a defect

P183.description: Explicitly check and handle every possible status code/return value, including unexpected ones, defaulting to fail-closed

P184.description: Catch and declare specific exception types rather than generic Exception/Throwable

P185.description: Release all held resources in a finally/cleanup block regardless of whether an exception was thrown

P186.description: Check for null/None before dereferencing any value that can legitimately be null or absent

P187.description: Include an explicit default/else branch in every switch/conditional chain, handling unexpected values safely

P188.description: Explicitly terminate every case block in a switch statement unless fallthrough is intentional and documented

P189.description: Configure custom error pages for all HTTP error codes so default server/framework error pages are never shown to users
